article_title: Thought Leadership Forum Brief: Turnaround Leadership and Leadership Competencies
citation: Center on School Turnaround at WestEd. (2018). Thought Leadership Forum Brief: Turnaround Leadership and Leadership Competencies. San Francisco, CA: WestEd. http://centeronschoolturnaround.org
title: University of Virginia Partnership for Leaders in Education turnaround competency model with four proficiency levels across seven competencies
description: An evidence-based competency model developed from analysis of the actions of successful turnaround principals, identifying competencies the analysis linked to improvements in student achievement. Table 1 presents seven competencies — including "Focuses on Sustainable Results," "Engages the Team," "Impact and Influence," and "Commitment to Student Learning" — each described across four levels of proficiency from basic to sustained, advanced behavior.
requirements: Assessment of a principal's competency levels within the model to enable districts to support growth in areas not yet strengths
constraints: The model addresses halting a school's performance decline, stabilizing the school, and initiating rapid upward trajectory in turnaround contexts
target_learners: Turnaround principals and the districts and states that select and develop them
target_learning_goals: Building leader competencies linked to student achievement gains in turnaround schools
examples: New Mexico's Principals Pursuing Excellence maps its program design elements to the competencies in this model
key_sources: Center on School Turnaround at WestEd. (2018). Thought Leadership Forum Brief: Turnaround Leadership and Leadership Competencies. San Francisco, CA: WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED592985

article_title: Improving performance and retention in introductory biology with a utility-value intervention.
citation: Canning, E. A., Harackiewicz, J. M., Priniski, S. J., Hecht, C. A., Tibbetts, Y., & Hyde, J. S. (2018). Improving Performance and Retention in Introductory Biology with a Utility-Value Intervention. Journal of educational psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000244
title: Time utility-value writing assignments to students' performance history: early for struggling students, late for high performers, with full dosage for the broadest benefit
description: The article's design recommendations follow from its timing and dosage findings: assignments asking students to explain why course material is useful to them personally should be scheduled deliberately across a course. The authors conclude that "full dosage (three UV assignments) is optimal to obtain the highest level of articulated UV, the beneficial early (first UV) effect on performance for low performers, and the beneficial late (3rd UV) effect on continuation for high performers." Because one or three doses worked but two did not, implementers should either commit to a dose for every unit or a single well-timed essay, not an arbitrary middle number.
requirements: Assignments must be graded for scientific content with feedback, and instructors kept blind to condition as in the study implementation.
UV prompts must ask students to explain how specific course content applies personally or to someone close to them, not merely summarize.
constraints: Two doses were not effective for performance or continuation in this study.

The timing moderation is exploratory: the early-benefit-for-low-performers effect on continuation did not reach significance (p = .063), and late UV may decrease enrollment for students more than 1 SD below the mean prior GPA.
Effects were tested in one introductory biology course at a large Midwestern university.
target_learners: Undergraduate students in introductory STEM gateway courses
examples: Students were blocked on gender and randomly assigned to a fully crossed 2×2×2 design in which each of three five-week unit essays was either a UV essay or a control summary, assigned three weeks before each unit exam.
key_sources: Canning, E. A., Harackiewicz, J. M., Priniski, S. J., Hecht, C. A., Tibbetts, Y., & Hyde, J. S. (2018). Improving Performance and Retention in Introductory Biology with a Utility-Value Intervention. Journal of educational psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000244

article_title: Communications and discussions: The organization of the Department of Education at the University of Vermont.
citation: Communications and Discussions. (1910). The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://eric.ed.gov
title: University of Vermont Department of Education organized so education strengthens teaching of other subjects
description: The Department of Education at the University of Vermont was organized around the premise that education study should serve teachers of other subjects rather than stand as an isolated elective. As Messenger writes, "The chief function of the department of education is to strengthen them as teachers of those subjects." Students completing two years of required work receive the Bachelor of Science in Education, and students enrolled in other departments may take education courses and have the words "in education" appended to their baccalaureate degree.
requirements: Students must have completed the first two years in any department of the University before entering the department of education
constraints: Admission to education courses by students enrolled elsewhere requires permission of the dean of the department in which he is enrolled and of the dean of the department of education
target_learners: Undergraduates preparing to teach elementary and secondary school subjects
College graduates who are not teachers but will hold positions on school boards and boards of trustees
target_learning_goals: Insight into educational tendencies found in other subjects
Strengthening subject-matter teachers with educational theory
examples: Students who have completed the first two years in any department may enter and receive the degree of Bachelor of Science in Education
Education courses are open as free electives to juniors and seniors in any department
key_sources: Communications and Discussions. (1910). The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://eric.ed.gov

article_title: Communications and discussions: The organization of the Department of Education at the University of Vermont.
citation: Communications and Discussions. (1910). The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://eric.ed.gov
title: Vermont education program pattern combining education courses, two outside subjects, secondary methods, and an educational thesis
description: The program's requirements interleave education study with subject-matter study across the degree. As printed: "The requirements of the department are: psychology; principles of instruction; history of education; one o^her full course in education," plus two courses in each of two subjects given in other departments, two courses in secondary methods, and free electives to reach at least fifteen hours per week. A thesis treating some subject studied in the University from the educational point of view must be accepted by both the subject professor and the dean of the department of education.
requirements: A thesis treating of some subject studied in the University, from the educational point of view, must be accepted by the professor who teaches the subject and by the dean of the department of education
constraints: Argumentation and debate are required of all students in the College of Liberal Arts and are excluded from the fifteen-hour weekly total
target_learners: Undergraduate students in the College of Liberal Arts preparing to teach
target_learning_goals: Teaching a school subject with grounding in psychology, instruction, history of education, and educational philosophy
examples: The one additional full education course is selected after conference with the dean of the department from the philosophy of education, genetic psychology, school administration and secondary education
key_sources: Communications and Discussions. (1910). The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://eric.ed.gov

article_title: Communications and discussions: The organization of the Department of Education at the University of Vermont.
citation: Communications and Discussions. (1910). The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://eric.ed.gov
title: Master's pattern splitting study between education and a specialization, with the thesis discussed in light of educational principles
description: At the master's level, the department pairs education study with disciplinary specialization. As printed: "A candidate for the master's degree is advised to devote about one-half of his time to the subject of education and the other half to some other subject in which he wishes to specialize." As a rule the thesis deals with the special subject, but the candidate is required to discuss it in the light of educational principles, extending the integration pattern of the undergraduate program.
requirements: The master's thesis must discuss the candidate's special subject in the light of educational principles
target_learners: Master's degree candidates specializing in a teaching subject
target_learning_goals: Applying educational principles to a specialized subject
examples: As a rule his thesis deals with his special subject, but he is required to discuss it in the light of educational principles
key_sources: Communications and Discussions. (1910). The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://eric.ed.gov

article_title: Promoting persistence in the biological and medical sciences: An expectancy-value approach to intervention.
citation: Hecht, C. A., Harackiewicz, J. M., Priniski, S. J., Canning, E. A., Tibbetts, Y., & Hyde, J. S. (2019). Promoting Persistence in the Biological and Medical Sciences: An Expectancy-Value Approach to Intervention. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000356
title: Utility-value writing assignments in an introductory biology course for biomedical majors
description: The intervention consisted of three graded writing assignments in the first course of a two-course introductory biology sequence. In both conditions students selected a lecture concept, formulated a question, and wrote a 1-2 page essay; UVI students additionally "discuss[ed] the relevance of the concept or issue to your own life" (essay variation) or wrote a letter connecting material to another person (letter variation). Assignments were cumulatively worth 1.8% of the course grade and were graded by biology graduate students for scientific accuracy.
requirements: Assignments were presented as graded course assignments within a gateway course taken by prospective biomedical majors, and instructional staff were blind to condition.
constraints: The article notes findings are limited to the context of the biomedical fields and to students who were all at least considering a biomedical major.
target_learners: undergraduate students in introductory biology, including first-generation and underrepresented minority students
target_learning_goals: reflection on personal relevance of course topics
examples: In a double-blind randomized controlled trial across four semesters, 2,378 students enrolled; the analyzed sample comprised 1,039 consenting students, with 579 assigned to the UVI condition and 460 to control.
key_sources: Hecht, C. A., Harackiewicz, J. M., Priniski, S. J., Canning, E. A., Tibbetts, Y., & Hyde, J. S. (2019). Promoting Persistence in the Biological and Medical Sciences: An Expectancy-Value Approach to Intervention. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000356
